properties.decision:
Recorded as brainstorming on 2026-09-20 from flo2's meta-point, not as a proposal. The reporter calls it the most useful thing in their addendum and they may be right.

THE MEASUREMENT: four things rebuilt that reflow2 already served, each filed upstream as 'reflow2 should add X'. The served instructions are 416 lines, name `get_skill` and `list_skills` twice between them, and name `find_tools` zero times. Both discoveries in the same addendum came from two find_tools calls once the reporter thought to make them.

OPTIONS.
(a) ONE LINE IN THE INSTRUCTIONS, their wording: 'before you build a capability against reflow2, search for it: find_tools takes a job description.' Cheapest by far, reaches every session unasked, and is the only option that acts before the work starts.
(b) DELIVER IT AT THE STEP instead, as a rule naming the moments a capability is proposed — the mechanism this project already uses for rules that kept being broken. COUNTER: the moment a CONSUMER decides to build something is not a moment reflow2 sees, which is the same limit the memory-boundary rule ran into.
(c) BOTH.
(d) NOTHING, on the grounds that an agent that believes it knows the surface will not search whatever it is told. COUNTER: untested here, and the cost of (a) is one sentence.

⚠️ WHAT THIS IS NOT, and the distinction matters: it is not that the tools are hard to find. Every served tool ranks for a job sentence and a held-out corpus proves it. It is that the one document every session receives unasked never says the catalogue exists.
properties.name: OPEN — should the served instructions tell a reader to ask whether a thing already exists before building it?
